newsitem.title: USA: Congressional panel issues draft of bank reform.
newsitem.headline: Congressional panel issues draft of bank reform.

text.p: Legislators working to overhaul antiquated U.S. banking laws issued a draft proposal late Tuesday for consideration by the House Banking committee next week.
The draft will form the basis of the banking panel's effort to pass a reform plan at a June 17 meeting, although committee chairman Jim Leach said the proposal could change again later this week.
If the proposal became law, the Iowa Republican said it would eliminate most of the Depression era laws separating banking from other financial services such as insurance and securities underwriting.

But Congress has debated bank reform proposals to scrap the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act for more than a decade. The initiatives have alays broken down when the major financial industries were unable to reach a consensus.
In a cover memo attached to the draft, Leach acknowledged the difficult task ahead and warned that the proposal would not please all sides.

"In the context of so many differing perspectives of self interest within and between industry groups and in the context of differing views of the public interest, the goal is not to satisfy all parties but to be as fair as possible to each and as advancing as possible of the public interest," Leach wrote.
Lawmakers opted not to include any language in the draft about whether banks should be allowed to venture farther afield and engage in commercial activities.
Numerous amendments are expected on the banking and commerce issue, ranging from an outright ban on any mixing to allowing unfettered combinations of banks and nonfinancial companies.
